subject: math
title: Sets, Relations and Functions
syllabus: Sets and their representation: Union, intersection and complement of sets and their algebraic properties; Power set; Relation, Type of relations, equivalence relations, functions; one-one, into and onto functions, the composition of functions.

body: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B). Three sets: add the pairs back, take the triple out again.
"Neither a multiple of p nor of q" in a range: total − ⌊multiples of p⌋ − ⌊multiples of q⌋ + ⌊multiples of lcm⌋.
Subsets of an n-set: 2^{n}. Subsets with no two consecutive numbers follow s_{n} = s_{n−1} + s_{n−2} (Fibonacci).
Splitting 3k objects into named groups of k: \f{(3k)!}{(k!)^{3}}; unnamed groups: divide by 3!.

body: A relation on A is any set of ordered pairs from A × A. Reflexive: every (a, a). Symmetric: (a, b) → (b, a). Transitive: (a, b), (b, c) → (a, c).
Equivalence = all three; it splits A into classes (partitions). Number of equivalence relations on a 3-set = 5.
On an n-set: all relations 2^{n²}; reflexive 2^{n² − n}; symmetric 2^{n(n+1)/2}; reflexive and symmetric 2^{n(n−1)/2}
"Fewest pairs to add": for reflexive, count the missing (a, a); for symmetric, count pairs whose reverse is missing.
Domain: √{·} needs ≥ 0 (> 0 in a denominator); log needs argument > 0 and base > 0, ≠ 1; sec^{−1}t needs |t| ≥ 1.
Range of y = f(x): solve for x and ask when a real x exists. For a quotient of quadratics, the discriminant in x gives an inequality in y.
Bounded pieces: \f{1}{c − sin kx} has range [\f{1}{c + 1}, \f{1}{c − 1}]; a sin x + b cos x lies in [−√{a^{2} + b^{2}}, √{a^{2} + b^{2}}].
One-one (injective): different inputs, different outputs — a strictly increasing or decreasing function is one-one. Onto: every element of the codomain is hit.
A quotient of two quadratics (denominator never 0) is never one-one and never onto R.
(fog)(x) = f(g(x)). If g is the inverse of f: f(a) = b ⟹ g(b) = a and g'(b) = \f{1}{f'(a)}.
Composing \f{kx}{√{1 + cx^{2}}} with itself n times keeps the same shape — track how the coefficient grows.

Onto: Σ_{k}(−1)^{k}C(n, k)(n − k)^{m}
Not onto = all − onto. Many-one = all − one-one. Fix the constrained values first, then fill the rest.

f(m + n) = f(m) + f(n) → f(n) = n f(1). f(x + y) = f(x)f(y) → f(x) = a^{x}.
When f is a polynomial: put x = 0 or y = 0 first, then compare coefficients.

formulas: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B)
traps: A relation can be symmetric and transitive without being reflexive (e.g. {(1,1)} on {1, 2}).
One-one onto depends on the codomain: e^{x} : R → R is not onto, but R → (0, ∞) is.
For log domains also check the base: > 0 and ≠ 1.
Many-one functions = all functions minus one-one, not minus onto.
"Fewest pairs for symmetry" counts missing reverses, not all pairs.
Equivalence relations on n elements = number of partitions (Bell number), not 2^{something}.

pyq.q: Let the set S = {2, 4, 8, 16, …, 512} be partitioned into 3 sets A, B, C with equal number of elements such that A ∪ B ∪ C = S and A ∩ B = B ∩ C = A ∩ C = ϕ. The maximum number of such possible partitions of S is equal to :
sol: S has 9 elements; A, B, C are named sets of 3 each.
Choose A: C(9, 3) = 84, then B: C(6, 3) = 20, C is what is left → 84 × 20 = 1680.

pyq.q: Let A = {n ∈ [100, 700] ∩ N : n is neither a multiple of 3 nor a multiple of 4}. Then the number of elements in A is ____.
For n ≥ 2, let S_{n} denote the set of all subsets of {1, 2, …, n} with no two consecutive numbers. For example {1, 3, 5} ∈ S_{6}, but {1, 2, 4} ∉ S_{6}. Then n(S_{5}) is equal to ____.
sol: Count by whether n is used: s_{n} = s_{n−1} + s_{n−2} (empty set included).

pyq.q: Let f : [0, 3] → A be defined by f(x) = 2x^{3} − 15x^{2} + 36x + 7 and g : [0, ∞) → B be defined by g(x) = \f{x^{2025}}{x^{2025} + 1}. If both the functions are onto and S = {x ∈ Z : x ∈ A or x ∈ B}, then n(S) is equal to:
sol: g takes values in [0, 1) → B = [0, 1). Integers: 7, …, 35 (29 of them) and 0 → 30.

pyq.q: Let A = {1, 2, 3, …, 100} and R be a relation on A such that R = {(a, b) : a = 2b + 1}. Let (a_{1}, a_{2}), (a_{2}, a_{3}), (a_{3}, a_{4}), …, (a_{k}, a_{k+1}) be a sequence of k elements of R such that the second entry of an ordered pair is equal to the first entry of the next ordered pair. Then the largest integer k, for which such a sequence exists, is equal to :
sol: Each step halves: a_{i+1} = \f{a_{i} − 1}{2}. Longest chain ends at 1.

pyq.q: Let A = {−2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3}. Let R be a relation on A defined by xRy if and only if y = max{x, 1}. Let l be the number of elements in R. Let m and n be the minimum number of elements required to be added in R to make it reflexive and symmetric relations, respectively. Then l + m + n is equal to
sol: Reflexive needs (−2,−2), (−1,−1), (0,0) → m = 3; symmetric needs (1,−2), (1,−1), (1,0) → n = 3. Total 12.

pyq.q: Let A = {−3, −2, −1, 0, 1, 2, 3} and R be a relation on A defined by xRy if and only if 2x − y ∈ {0, 1}. Let l be the number of elements in R. Let m and n be the minimum number of elements required to be added in R to make it reflexive and symmetric relations, respectively. Then l + m + n is equal to :
sol: Missing diagonal pairs: 5 → m = 5; missing reverses of the 5 off-diagonal pairs → n = 5. Total 17.

pyq.q: Let a relation R on N × N be defined as : (x_{1}, y_{1})R(x_{2}, y_{2}) if and only if x_{1} ≤ x_{2} or y_{1} ≤ y_{2}. Consider the two statements : (I) R is reflexive but not symmetric. (II) R is transitive. Then which one of the following is true?
sol: Reflexive: x ≤ x. Not symmetric: (1,1)R(2,2) but not (2,2)R(1,1).
Not transitive: (2,3)R(3,1) (2 ≤ 3) and (3,1)R(1,2) (1 ≤ 2), but (2,3) is not related to (1,2). Only (I).

pyq.q: Let the relations R_{1} and R_{2} on the set X = {1, 2, 3, …, 20} be given by R_{1} = {(x, y) : 2x − 3y = 2} and R_{2} = {(x, y) : −5x + 4y = 0}. If M and N be the minimum number of elements required to be added in R_{1} and R_{2}, respectively, in order to make the relations symmetric, then M + N equals ____.

Let A = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. Let R be a relation on A defined by (x, y) ∈ R if and only if max{x, y} ∈ {3, 4}. Then among the statements (S_{1}) : The number of elements in R is 18, and (S_{2}) : The relation R is symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive
sol: Symmetric (max is symmetric); (0,0) ∉ R → not reflexive; (0,3), (3,0) ∈ R but (0,0) ∉ R → not transitive. S_{2} true.

pyq.q: Let A = {2, 3, 6, 8, 9, 11} and B = {1, 4, 5, 10, 15}. Let R be a relation on A × B defined by (a, b)R(c, d) if and only if 3ad − 7bc is an even integer. Then the relation R is
sol: Mod 2: 3ad − 7bc ≡ ad + bc, which is symmetric in the two pairs; (a,b) with itself gives 2ab — even → reflexive.
o: reflexive and symmetric but not transitive.

pyq.q: Let A = {2, 3, 6, 7} and B = {4, 5, 6, 8}. Let R be a relation defined on A × B by (a_{1}, b_{1})R(a_{2}, b_{2}) if and only if a_{1} + a_{2} = b_{1} + b_{2}. Then the number of elements in R is ____.
sol: Count quadruples a_{1} + a_{2} = b_{1} + b_{2}: tabulate the sums of A + A and of B + B.

pyq.q: The number of relations, defined on the set {a, b, c, d}, which are both reflexive and symmetric, is equal to:
sol: Diagonal pairs are forced; the 6 unordered off-diagonal pairs are taken or left together.

pyq.q: Let A = {2, 3, 4, 5, 6}. Let R be a relation on the set A × A given by (x, y)R(z, w) if and only if x divides z and y ≤ w. Then the number of elements in R is ____.
sol: Pairs (y, w) with y ≤ w: 15. Total 8 × 15 = 120.

pyq.q: Let A = {2, 3, 5, 7, 9}. Let R be the relation on A defined by xRy if and only if 2x ≤ 3y. Let l be the number of elements in R, and m be the minimum number of elements required to be added in R to make it a symmetric relation. Then l + m is equal to :
sol: List R: every (x, y) with y ≥ \f{2x}{3} → 19 pairs.
6 of them lack their reverse → l + m = 25.

pyq.q: The number of non-empty equivalence relations on the set {1, 2, 3} is :
sol: Equivalence relations ↔ partitions of the set.

pyq.q: Let A = {1, 2, 3}. The number of relations on A, containing (1, 2) and (2, 3), which are reflexive and transitive but not symmetric, is ____.
sol: Adding nothing works. Adding (2,1) alone or (3,2) alone keeps it transitive (and still not symmetric).
Any other addition forces enough pairs to make it the full (symmetric) relation → 3.

pyq.q: Let X = R × R. Define a relation R on X as : (a_{1}, b_{1})R(a_{2}, b_{2}) ⟺ b_{1} = b_{2}. Statement I: R is an equivalence relation. Statement II : For some (a, b) ∈ X, the set S = {(x, y) ∈ X : (x, y)R(a, b)} represents a line parallel to y = x.
sol: "Same second coordinate" is reflexive, symmetric and transitive → equivalence.
S = {(x, y) : y = b} is a horizontal line, never parallel to y = x → II false.
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

sol: x + x is even → reflexive; symmetric clearly.
x + y and y + z even → x, y, z same parity → x + z even → transitive. Equivalence.

pyq.q: The function f : (−∞, ∞) → (−∞, 1), defined by f(x) = \f{2^{x} − 2^{−x}}{2^{x} + 2^{−x}} is :
sol: f is tanh(x ln 2): strictly increasing → one-one.
Its values stay in (−1, 1), so values ≤ −1 in the codomain (−∞, 1) are missed → not onto.

pyq.q: For the function f : [1, ∞) → [1, ∞) defined by f(x) = (x − 1)^{4} + 1, among the two statements: (I) The set S = {x ∈ [1, ∞) : f(x) = f^{−1}(x)} contains exactly two elements, and (II) The set S = {x ∈ [1, ∞) : f(x) = f^{−1}(x + 1)} is an empty set,
sol: f is increasing, so f(x) = f^{−1}(x) ⟺ f(x) = x ⟺ (x − 1)^{4} = x − 1 → x = 1 or 2: exactly two (I true).
f^{−1}(x + 1) = 1 + x^{1/4}; (x − 1)^{4} = x^{1/4} has a root between 2 and 3 → S is not empty (II false).

sol: Denominator never zero; f → \f{2}{3} at ±∞ and dips below it, so values repeat → not one-one.
